charts.annotation: Global Specialty (Innovative Medicines -- Ilumya, Winlevi, Cequa, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) is cross-cutting within the US/EM/RoW totals above, not additive to them; it is the line management calls out as ~22% of consolidated sales and the segment renamed from "Specialty" to "Global Specialty" in FY2026.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentMixIndia.title: India formulations and API revenue
segmentMixIndia.content:
India Formulations is Sun Pharma's branded-generics business sold to Indian pharmacies, hospitals and physicians -- its largest and most defensive segment. API is bulk active-pharmaceutical-ingredient sales to third-party drugmakers, a lower-margin, capacity-driven business distinct from the company's own formulations.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: India is ~33% of consolidated sales and is growing via Tier-II/III pharmacy expansion, 14-19 new product launches a quarter, and entry into the GLP-1 category (Noveltreat, Sematrinity); external API sales are growing ~12-14% YoY in recent quarters, supporting the formulations business rather than competing with it.

What to watch:

  • India growth outpacing the broader Indian pharma market (branded-generics pricing power)
  • API growing faster than formulations, which would signal spare capacity rather than demand pull

segmentMixGlobal.title: US, Emerging Markets, Rest of World and Global Specialty revenue
segmentMixGlobal.content:
Reported in US dollars (not rupees, unlike the rest of this dashboard). US Formulations mixes commoditised, price-eroding generics with the faster-growing Innovative Medicines specialty book. Emerging Markets and Rest of World are the remaining international formulations geographies. Global Specialty is the Innovative Medicines product line (Ilumya, Winlevi, Cequa, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) sold across all three geographies -- it is cross-cutting, not a fourth geography, so it should not be summed with the other three bars.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: management's thesis is a mix shift from low-margin US generics toward Global Specialty, now ~22% of consolidated sales and growing on new launches (LEQSELVI, UNLOXCYT in FY26) and Ilumya's new psoriatic-arthritis indication; EM/RoW growth is helped by currency tailwinds and stronger commercial infrastructure in Brazil and Romania. The segment was renamed from "Specialty" to "Global Specialty" in FY2026 -- the series is continuous through the rename.

What to watch:

  • Global Specialty growing faster than the US generics base it is supposed to offset
  • US Formulations flat or declining while Global Specialty (within it) still grows -- the generics erosion the mix shift is meant to mask

exceptionalItems.title: Exceptional items
exceptionalItems.content:
Exceptional items are one-off gains, provisions or litigation/settlement charges Sun Pharma discloses separately from underlying operations -- they swing reported EBITDA and net income in the quarter or year they land, independent of the business's run-rate.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: this line has been large and lumpy -- a roughly ₹39.4bn exceptional item in Q4 FY2022 and a step-up to ₹13.1bn for full-year FY2026 -- so a single quarter's EBITDA or net income move should be checked against this chart before reading it as operating performance.

What to watch:

  • Reported EBITDA/net income moves that are really an exceptional item, not demand
  • Litigation and US generics pricing-related provisions recurring year after year rather than being truly one-off

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
